notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 28% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the third-lowest in the league (a typical team: 39%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Filip Chytil is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Tom Willander is day to day (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Zeev Buium has taken his spot beside Jamie Oleksiak.
Jacob Quillan was added to the roster on Oct 31 and has played beside Linus Karlsson and Drew O'Connor.
Max Sasson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 18 games, up from 4% last season.

Zach Hyman is on injured reserve (neck injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is a top-six forward. Colton Dach has taken his spot beside Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Kasperi Kapanen. That line has had 59% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 46:04 together.

Matt Savoie is on long-term injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has not played this season. Leon Draisaitl has taken his spot beside Connor McDavid and Vasily Podkolzin. That line has had 63% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 201:12 together.
Matt Tomkins was added to the roster on Oct 24.
Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 52% of the team’s power-play time in 17 games, up from 6% last season.
Ty Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 13 games, down from 30% last season.

stakes: The Canucks go in eighth in the Pacific with 7 points, 18 points behind the Oilers, first.

EDM.head: The Oilers should be in control
EDM.body: Even though Edmonton will be without Hyman, the Oilers have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. If the Canucks want to spoil it, start with getting good looks.

VAN.head: A steep climb for the Canucks
VAN.body: Even though Edmonton will be without Hyman, the Oilers have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. To pull this off, the Canucks can start with getting good looks, plus Leevi Meriläinen stealing the show.

story.head: McDavid’s favorite opponent
paras: The teams have split two meetings this season. The Oilers (11-3-3) lost 5-4 to Anaheim on Thursday, and the Canucks are on a four-game losing streak. Going in, the Canucks are last in the NHL and the Oilers first in the Pacific (tied for third in the NHL).

The Canucks haven’t played well, but their record (.194) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .323, mostly because they’re 2-5 in one-goal games. The Oilers’ record (.735) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.591), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Canucks pick their shots (lowest) and have had shaky goaltending (32nd). They also have a leaky penalty kill (32nd), so the Oilers’ power play (2nd) could do real damage when they’re shorthanded. Vancouver has allowed 4.61 goals a game, the most in the league. On the other side, the Oilers lean on their stars more than any team in the league (lowest), have one of the league’s most dangerous power plays (2nd) and get their defensemen shooting (3rd). Edmonton has scored 4.12 goals a game, the most in the league. Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one.

Elias Pettersson (#40) (4 G / 14 A / 18 P in 18 GP) leads the Canucks in scoring. Brock Boeser (6 G / 9 A / 15 P in 18 GP) has a team-high six goals, with ten goals in twelve games against Edmonton since 2023-24. Connor McDavid (10 G / 34 A / 44 P in 17 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with ten points in his last five games and a point in eight straight games against Vancouver. Leon Draisaitl (14 G / 17 A / 31 P in 17 GP) has a team-high 14 goals, second in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games.
Leevi Meriläinen (2-6-1 / .889 SV% in 10 GS) will likely start for Vancouver, and Matt Tomkins (1-1-0 / .878 SV% in 2 GS) for Edmonton.
